title: "10 Meta-epidemiological study"
link-citations: true

Alternative labels: analytical study of applied methods

## Definition and typical features 
Meta-epidemiological studies draw on the same sources as reviews of applied methods, but they focus on how variation in methodological practice relates to variation in study results or other outcomes, analogous to how epidemiologists examine relationships between exposures and health outcomes. Researchers typically assemble a stratified or matched sample of studies that applied either of two or more alternative methods and use meta-regression to quantify differences in the corresponding results. The analysis typically requires multi-level modelling in one or two steps. 

- A strength is that these studies reflect real-world applications of methods, including human error. 
- A limitation is the high risk of confounding, which can arise at multiple levels, including differences in study populations, research questions, or measurement procedures.
